title: Threaded scheduler coda - weekly notes (threading, KV warmup, microbatch experiments)
body:
Week: 2029-03-25 -> 2029-03-29
Meeting: Serving Runtime weekly sync (threaded-scheduler breakout) — 2029-03-29 10:00 PT
Attendees: Maya P., Diego M., Rina C., Evan B., Sofia A., oncall: J. Park (partial)
Purpose: consolidate progress on the threaded scheduler prototype, KV-prefix warmup trials, and microbatch sizing heuristics; decide rollout guardrails and immediate safety checks for canary.

TL;DR:
- Threaded scheduler prototype (v0.3) reduces p99 token-generation tail by ~18% on the 8k-workload in local perf harness but increases average CPU context-switch counts; still within thermal/host limits.
- KV-prefix warmup (shadow warmup) yields ~12% fewer cold KVs for long conversations; memory overhead modest (peak +3% in arena).
- Adaptive microbatch sizing (alpha) shows 6–10% cost reduction for medium concurrency (200–800 RPS); under low-concurrency it regresses latency vs fixed small-batches.

Notes / Deep-dive:
1) Threaded scheduler (v0.3) update
   - What changed: moved worker-affinity from coarse groups -> fine-grained windowed threads; introduced per-thread run-queue with light stealing; added a deferred-completion ring to avoid blocking the critical path when small forward ops finish.
   - Benchmarks (perf harness, model: rw-large-08k, seq=1024):
       * Baseline (v0.2): p50=42ms, p90=72ms, p99=190ms, throughput=860 tok/s
       * v0.3 (threaded): p50=40ms, p90=68ms, p99=156ms, throughput=890 tok/s
       * Notes: p99 improvement concentrated in tail requests that experienced GC-like stalls in host scheduling under mixed load.
   - Observed side-effects: syscall frequency uptick (~+22%); on some hosts we saw small increases in CPU temperature spikes during long runs — infra asked to throttle one host to reproduce.
   - Open action: Diego to add per-thread telemetry (latency histograms by run-queue length) — due 2029-04-04.

2) KV-prefix warmup (shadow warming)
   - Approach: keep a lightweight shadow-worker that replays recent prefixes (last 3 tokens of active sessions) to pre-populate KV sets without affecting main latency. Avoid priming very long prefixes to cap cost.
   - Results from 48-hour canary on staging (mixed chat corpus): cold-hit ratio dropped from 0.19 -> 0.17; observed ~12% fewer 5-10ms cache misses per 10k requests. Memory consumption: resident +3% on average; peak +7% on pathological dumps.
   - Failure modes: under sudden traffic spike (3x baseline) warmup jobs compete with real requests for NVMe I/O on host; we need IO-limits.
   - Decision: enable shadow warmup on Dedicated pools with IO QoS only. Rule: warmup threads cap to 10% CPU and IO throttle to 5MB/s per device.
   - Open action: Rina to file infra ticket (SERV-2154) to add device-level IO throttles and test harness for warmup-induced interference. ETA 2029-04-08.

3) Adaptive microbatch sizing experiments
   - Idea: choose batch-size at request ingress using a small policy model that estimates request concurrency and predicted latency-sensitivity.
   - Alpha results (A/B vs fixed 8-token microbatch):
       * Medium concurrency (200–800 rps): cost per token -8%; median latency similar; p99 improved marginally.
       * Low concurrency (<50 rps): median latency worsened by ~6ms (due to batching delay).
   - Risk: heuristic misclassification can add batching delay for latency-sensitive customers.
   - Mitigation: add client-provided hint header (x-rdwd-latency-mode) we respect; default policy remains conservative (favor small batches when uncertain).
   - Open action: Evan to prototype policy fallback that enforces hard max batching-delay of 4ms for premium tiers. Target 2029-04-05.

4) Canary and rollout plan
   - Canary release plan for threaded scheduler + KV warmup on a small Dedicated pool (3 nodes):
       * Day 0: deploy v0.3 to pool, shadow warmup enabled in read-only mode; collect telemetry 24h.
       * Day 1: enable warmup active with IO QoS; run synthetic tail tests and compare; if p99 regresses >5% abort.
       * Day 3: expand to 10 nodes if stable.
   - Gate metrics: p50/p90/p99, CPU temp spikes, background syscall rate, KV cold-hit ratio, NVMe IO contention.
   - Rollback criteria: any p99 regression >8% for 3 consecutive hours or NVMe error rates increase by >0.5% above baseline.

5) Operational notes & playbook edits
   - Added quick check: `rdwctl sched thread-stats` to dump per-thread queue sizes (helpful in incident triage).
   - Updated playbook section 'Warmup interference' with steps to throttle/disable warmup on affected hosts and add an alert when warmup IO > 7MB/s per device.
   - Suggestion: embed warmup telemetry into Console (per-route) so SRE can see warmup impact on a per-customer basis. Filed as product request (PRD stub link in Confluence page).

6) Blockers / outstanding questions
   - Need infra assistance to reproduce NVMe contention: who can loan a host with synthetic IO throttling? (Action: SRE to allocate host pool — pinged infra on slack).
   - Do we want warmup enabled for hosted-api free-tier? likely no, but need product signoff. (Action: Maya to bring to product sync 2029-04-03).
   - Kernel handshake: a small race-case reported when a thread steals a queue while its deferred-completion ring still processing — low repro rate but must be fixed before wide rollout. (Diego owns fix, PR in progress).

7) Quick wins for next week
   - Add per-thread histograms (Diego).
   - IO throttling test harness + infra ticket (Rina).
   - Hard max batching-delay for premium lanes (Evan).
   - Product sync for warmup policy on tiers (Maya).

Misc / Notes to self:
- Small anecdote: observed one long customer session where warmup saved ~120ms over full conversation (nice win for user experience).
- Keep an eye on syscall growth — if it exceeds +30% we should consider consolidating threads or moving some work into userland co-routines.

Attachments / references (in doc):
- Perf logs: /archive/perf/2029-03-threaded-scheduler-v0.3 (internal)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8912
- Jira: SERV-2129 (threaded scheduler), SERV-2154 (warmup IO throttles)

Next meeting: 2029-04-05 (follow-up on telemetry additions and infra repro)

-- Maya
